clue.text: Daily set back for timekeeper not a night-worker

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: set back tells us the word for set is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to set something down is to have laid it

explanation.surface: A newspaper is postponed for someone who keeps time but refuses to work nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAID into DIAL. A sundial reads only by sunlight, so it never works at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the hour by the sun's shadow, so it is a clock that only operates during daylight.

clue.text: Splash through wet roads, a diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends traffic a different route, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A car splashes through wet roads on a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' rearranges WETROADSA. A 'splash' is a dash of soda added to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash in a whisky is a small dash of fizzy mixer.

clue.text: Girl cutting fabric

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name
a keen blade is sharp, i.e. cutting

explanation.surface: A girl is snipping some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Drunk in east by British — swallowed about one

indicators.note: about places the word for swallowed next to the numeral, with one coming just before it

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
I is the Roman numeral one
to have swallowed is to have ate

explanation.surface: A drunk in the East End beside a Briton gulped down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets the pieces side by side; 'about' puts I alongside ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard; as an adjective it means intoxicated.

clue.text: The French way to carry on

parts.note: la is the French feminine for 'the'
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The French have their own way of continuing.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to endure or continue going.

clue.text: Eccentric, like station sergeant

explanation.surface: An odd person resembles the police sergeant who stays at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: A police officer patrolling is 'on the beat'; a station sergeant behind the desk is off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional or quirky behaviour is called this; and a desk sergeant at the police station is not out on patrol.

clue.text: Excessive price for restaurant extra with no starter

indicators.note: with no starter means the first letter of the restaurant word is dropped

parts.note: a cover charge is an extra levied per diner at a restaurant

explanation.surface: A restaurant adds a steep surcharge even when you skip the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it means the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcharge is to demand too much money, so as a noun it is an inflated bill.

clue.text: Latest news about university flats perhaps

indicators.note: about means the musical letters go around the abbreviation for university

parts.note: F, D, G and E are notes, any of which can be flattened

explanation.surface: Recent reports concern student flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' suggests apartments; here it is musical notes. The fudge is a newspaper's stop-press column for late news.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers, the fudge was the space kept for last-minute stop-press items.

clue.text: Pick on journalist and put in place

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to elect is to pick
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a reporter and installs them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone elected has been voted into office.

clue.text: Bloomer made by trainee — one in position on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards
in places the two letters inside the word for position

parts.note: to put something is to position it
I is the Roman numeral one
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee makes a blunder while climbing to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flower. I and L inside PUT make PILUT, which 'on the way up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that blooms, and the tulip is a classic spring flower.

clue.text: Writer drawing from Chaucer and Lawrence

parts.note: Spenser called the poet 'Dan Chaucer', Dan being an old title meaning master
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: An author takes inspiration from two great English writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing from' is a link: the title 'Dan' comes from Chaucer and the initials 'T.E.' from Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine poet who wrote the Divine Comedy is a celebrated author.

clue.text: Hurry and come up, Veronica

parts.note: to hurry is to speed
water or tears well up, i.e. come up

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to rush over and appear, addressed by the name Veronica.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus of small blue-flowered plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the Latin genus name for the plants commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Query surrounding stray vessel

indicators.note: surrounding says the question word wraps around the word for stray

parts.note: why is a query
to stray is to err

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question about a wandering boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge, a kind of craft for water.

clue.text: Cap for a prison officer

parts.note: a warder is slang 'screw', so a cap for one is that word's top; but the phrase also means a lid that twists on

explanation.surface: Headgear is issued to a warder.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is British prison slang for a warder; the cap that sits on top of a screw is the twist-on lid of a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded lid that is twisted onto a jar or bottle is named after its spiral fit.

clue.text: Give sound evidence of friction in cricket

definitions.text: Give sound evidence of friction in cricket

parts.words: Give sound evidence of friction in cricket
parts.note: reads like a cricket match dispute, but means the chirping an insect makes by rubbing its legs

explanation.surface: Testimony about tension in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket suggests the British bat-and-ball game, but here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects chirp by rubbing body parts together, a shrill sound named from Latin for creaking.

clue.text: Transport found in Hatton Garden

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters sit inside the words Hatton Garden

explanation.surface: Some vehicle turns up in London's jewellery district.
explanation.walkthrough: Hatton Garden is London's diamond and jewellery quarter. A tonga is a light horse-drawn carriage used in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a two-wheeled horse carriage of the Indian subcontinent, a form of conveyance.

clue.text: Awful display of greed at an outdoor restaurant

indicators.note: an awful display of the letters means they are set out in a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: Diners at an open-air cafe behave greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful display of' jumbles GREEDATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden where refreshments and tea are served outside is an open-air eating place.

clue.text: Slander typical of cat, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: as a Persian is a typical cat, the phrase 'as Persian' fits

explanation.surface: Defamation is said to be typical of cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as Persian', said aloud, matches the word for slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting aspersions means making damaging remarks about someone's character.

clue.text: Minimal changes in sea levels, despite an upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval throws the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: Sea levels barely change despite a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' reorders DESPITEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Neaps are the tides with the smallest range between high and low water.

clue.text: Call again about finish — of the building?

indicators.note: about here means the phone-call word goes around the word for finish

parts.note: to call again on the phone is to re-ring
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone phones back about completing a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: rendering is the plaster finish coating a building's walls, so 'finish' does its work in the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering is a coat of plaster or cement applied to a building's exterior walls.

clue.text: Quarrel between partners in difficult straits possibly

indicators.note: between means the bolt word sits between the two bridge players

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A row between partners leaves them in tricky circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like a row; it is a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel of water that is hard to navigate is called this.

clue.text: Leave with a garment

parts.note: to park a car is to leave it

explanation.surface: Someone goes away taking a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Complaining outright would be sickening

parts.note: read as 'out right': with R for right taken out, the word becomes the sickening one
falling ill is sickening, or ailing

explanation.surface: Grumbling openly would make one ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'outright' as 'out R': remove the R and what remains means sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something is to protest bitterly about it.

clue.text: "…casements, opening on the foam of seas" (Keats)

definitions.text: casements, opening on the foam of seas" (Keats)

parts.words: casements, opening on the foam of seas" (Keats)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing: the gap before 'seas' in the Nightingale ode is the answer

explanation.surface: A line from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote of 'magic casements, opening on the foam / Of perilous seas, in faery lands forlorn'; the solver supplies the missing adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective Keats used for the seas means dangerous, full of risk.

clue.text: River god of the frozen north perhaps

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a Lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A river deity rules the icy north.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic regions round the pole are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Failure when no points secured by either side

indicators.note: secured by means the middle letters are held between the outer pair

parts.note: L and R are left and right, either side
O looks like a zero, no score
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: A loser is someone who fails when neither team scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is unsuccessful, beaten in a contest, is called this.

clue.text: Stir at reappearance of skilled performer

indicators.note: the letters of the two words reappear in a different order

explanation.surface: A gifted entertainer causes a commotion on returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reappearance of' reshuffles STIRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste or artist is someone accomplished in a creative craft or entertainment.

clue.text: Circular letter to writer is unsealed

parts.note: O is the round letter
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A circular sent to an author arrives without its envelope sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' suggests a mailshot; here it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope that is not stuck down is not closed.

clue.text: Be quick to see and sign on staff

parts.note: to look is to see
a sharp is a musical sign written on the staff or stave

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry, observe and register as an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but it is the five-line musical stave on which a sharp sign is written.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up, move smartly.

clue.text: I competed clad in green

parts.note: to vie is to compete, so competed is vied

explanation.surface: Someone took part in a contest dressed in green.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall overgrown with ivy is covered in green climbing foliage.

clue.text: Book substitute player

explanation.surface: Someone books a replacement on the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table is to secure it in advance; and a substitute on a team waits on the bench.

clue.text: Worry in Opposition short of majorities

indicators.note: in places the word for worry inside the votes against

parts.note: noes are votes cast in opposition
to nag is to worry at someone

explanation.surface: Concern grows among the opposition, lacking a majority in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majorities' suggests votes, but it means coming of age; being short of that is legal minority.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the period of being under legal age, before reaching adulthood.
